method: Queried the visible h1 (text 'Inbox', filtered against the invisible no-JS fallback h1) and the task <ul> (identified by containing a checkbox with aria-label starting 'Mark task'). Walked getBoundingClientRect() up the ancestor chain from both, and separately computed their DOM common ancestor.

domCommonAncestorOfH1AndList.note: This is the naive DOM common ancestor of the h1 and the <ul> -- NOT the content column. It is wider than the wrapper this run's own earlier mistake (1190px 'main' region) but still the wrong element: same class of error the ledger already flags.

h1AncestorChain.note: width jumps back to 1175 here -- the 800px cap is applied to depths 1-3 only, a header-row wrapper, not to this or any higher ancestor

listAncestorChain.note: width jumps back to 1175 here -- the 800px cap on the list side ends at section_list, one level below this

finding: Todoist does not realise the '800px content column' as one DOM element wrapping both the h1 and the list. The h1 sits inside its own 800px-wide wrapper (depths 1-3 above, left ~462-467, right ~1262-1267) and the task list sits inside a SEPARATE 800px-wide wrapper (list_holder/section/section_list, left 467.5, right 1267.5) -- both nested inside a shared 1175px 'project_view' ancestor (main-view-layout is 1190px, one level further out). The two 800px wrappers align to the same visual column (edges agree within ~5px) even though they are not one shared DOM node.

measurement.source: list's own section_list wrapper (depth 4 from <ul>), the tighter and more consistent of the two 800px readings

verdictAgainstLedger: Confirms the ~800px figure the row expects (not the 1190px main region an earlier run captured), but corrects the row's own framing: there is no single 'content column' element containing both the h1 and the list on Todoist's side -- it is two independently 800px-capped siblings under a wider 1175px container. meologue, by contrast, really does use one wrapping element for both (flow6: 800px, left 499, right 1299) -- so this is a structural divergence in HOW the two apps achieve the same visual column width, not just a pixel value to compare.
